items.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I had an old record with Kit Howard when he did “I Wish I Could Shimmy Like My Sister Kate,”

ctx.x: What kind of tunes did you call at that time?

Well quite naturally, we did “Milenberg’s Joy,” that’s the first song we did. I kind of knew it. I didn’t really know the melody but it was kind of like “Bourbon Street” form so I could follow it. And I had an old record with Kit Howard when he did “I Wish I Could Shimmy Like My Sister Kate,” and “Sugar Blues,” “What Can I Say Dear After I Say I’m Sorry,” what else was on that — oh “Coconut Island.” Songs like this. It was a wide array of songs. And Papa was like, “Yeah man, you’re doing good man.” And I knew a…
All right. At that point, how old were you, 1976?
